summary: BA's plan addresses 11 of 13 bugs but defers Bug 4 entirely (no code change this cycle) and reduces Bug 10 to a no-op (no renderer changes for attractions/shopping/entertainment). Both decisions narrow the user's verbatim 'all-at-once' directive beyond what evidence supports. Bug 4's user-visible mitigation (split _merge_day_data into helpers under scripts/lib/) is technically achievable this cycle and was explicitly recommended in user's own RCA prose at spec-20260513-085358 line 159 ('拆 generate-html-interactive.py 把 _merge_day_data 拆 helpers'). Bug 10's user-named root cause ('所有混乱的根源') deserves at least a schema-migration scaffold worker, not pure deferral. Additionally, AC1/AC3 verification recipes require live browser screenshots without a runnable text-grep fallback, creating PASS_AS_SUBSTITUTE risk in the next cycle. W1->W2 env-var coupling is fragile and lacks an orchestrator-side hard gate. Evidence quality for the 11 in-scope bugs is solid (line-number anchors verified by sample-read of generate-html-interactive.py:643, :470-508, :2770-2781; pretool-quality-gate.py 0 BYPASS hits confirmed; budget.json trip_total=23416 vs sum=13044 confirmed; meals.json Day 12 alternatives 沈大成/光明邨 confirmed; generate-and-deploy.sh argv-parser reproduced). BA must re-plan to either include Bug 4 + Bug 10 fixes or escalate the scope-narrowing decision to the user for explicit approval.

objections.claim: AC1 literal text: 'screenshot captured at desktop 1440x900: docs/dev/screenshots/20260513-090000/ac1-desktop.png AND screenshot captured at mobile 390x844: docs/dev/screenshots/20260513-090000/ac1-mobile.png'. AC3 literal text: 'AND screenshot evidence at desktop + mobile captured'. No text-grep or curl fallback is specified.
objections.evidence_against: If QA in the next cycle cannot reach Playwright (e.g., the orchestrator dispatches QA without browser tooling), the literal recipe is unrunnable. The cycle then either FAILs (no screenshots = AC unmet) or PASS_AS_SUBSTITUTEs (QA verifies a different recipe than the AC declares). Both outcomes are bad. The minimum-safe AC text should declare BOTH a primary live-browser recipe AND a text-grep fallback recipe so QA can always produce evidence at the AC's literal level: AC1 fallback: `curl https://travel.life-ai.app/china/2026-04-12/ | grep -E '沈大成|光明邨'` MUST return >= 2 distinct matches in the Timeline View HTML region. AC3 fallback: same curl, grep for 'Unscheduled' or 'Optional' section heading + the optional item's name_local.
objections.required_fix: Amend AC1 to add: 'Fallback verification (text-only): curl <deployed-url> | grep -c "沈大成" returns >= 1 AND grep -c "光明邨" returns >= 1 in the Timeline View section. Live-browser screenshot is preferred evidence; text-grep is acceptable when browser tooling is unavailable.' Amend AC3 similarly. Update context-20260513-090000.json success_criteria to mirror.
objections.codex_concurrence: Q5 — codex marked 'AC must require real desktop + mobile browser screenshots, not grep/curl'; QA partially disagrees and requires BOTH (live primary + text fallback) to avoid PASS_AS_SUBSTITUTE.

objections.claim: BA's W1->W2 sequencing relies on the orchestrator setting BYPASS_QUALITY_GATE=1 in W2's dispatch environment. BA's only mitigation is 'W1 worker tests BYPASS by attempting a no-op Edit on the renderer file as part of its acceptance' — this verifies the gate wiring, NOT that the orchestrator will actually set the env-var for W2.
objections.evidence_against: If the orchestrator forgets the env-var (which is a coordination contract NOT enforced anywhere in the cycle's diff), W2 dev-worker will get blocked on the quality-gate on its first Edit. BA's spec leaves this enforcement gap unfilled. The fragility is asymmetric: W1 succeeds (wires the env-var read), W2 fails to even start. The cycle stalls.
objections.required_fix: BA must add either (a) an explicit orchestrator-contract clause to context-20260513-090000.json specifying that the dispatch prompt for W2 MUST include 'BYPASS_QUALITY_GATE=1 must be set in your shell environment before any Edit on scripts/generate-html-interactive.py' AND a verification step — OR (b) make the BYPASS auto-detect based on a sentinel file (e.g., .claude/dev-registry/dev-20260513-090000/qa.json existence) so W2 doesn't depend on env-var coordination. Option (a) is simpler. Either way, the dependency must be explicit, not implicit.
objections.codex_concurrence: Q4 — codex marked 'Yes, fragile. W1->W2 env-var coupling needs a documented contract plus tests'.

objections.claim: BA's Bug 7 evidence section says: 'while [ "$#" -gt 1 ] then case "$1" without initial shift; $1 remains PLAN_ID if user passes bash generate-and-deploy.sh <plan> --day 1-5, so --day is never matched.' The spec-20260513-085358 Section 1 line 29 and cp-state-qa.json cp-05 both say '--day flag silently ignored'.
objections.evidence_against: Live reproduction (QA verified): running `bash scripts/generate-and-deploy.sh foo --day 1-5` produces '❌ Error: Unknown option foo' AND exits 1 (NOT silent). The case fall-through hits `*) echo Error; exit 1`. The user-visible symptom is 'loud error, exits 1' — not 'silently ignored'. BA's prose description correctly identifies the mechanism (no initial shift) but the failure mode characterization carried from spec/cp-state is inaccurate.
objections.required_fix: Update BA spec evidence-section for Bug 7 to: 'No initial shift before option loop. Result: when user runs `bash deploy.sh <plan> --day 1-5`, $1=plan-id, case falls through to *), prints "Unknown option <plan-id>", exits 1 (loud error, not silent).' Update AC6 expected behavior to assert exit code 0 AND --day forwarded. This is minor (BA's mechanism is right; only the symptom phrasing drifts) but worth correcting before dev acts on the inaccurate prior context.
objections.codex_concurrence: Not surveyed (Q-set didn't cover Bug 7 specifically).

BA's spec edge-case discussion warns about this but doesn't bind W3 to fix it. W3's constraint section only says 'Resolve absolute-symlink portability issue: prefer relative symlink OR migrate path constant'.
objections.evidence_against: QA verified: ls -la .claude/skills/google-maps confirms it points to /root/travel-planner/.claude/commands/scripts/google-maps (absolute, non-portable across checkouts). If W3 chooses 'commit-symlink' branch without first converting to relative, the cycle ships a non-portable artifact. BA's spec leaves the branch choice to the dev worker; AC5 only requires 'no FileNotFoundError on clean checkout' which can be satisfied by either branch but only the relative-symlink branch is durable.
objections.required_fix: Tighten AC5 to require: 'EITHER (a) the symlink at .claude/skills/google-maps is REPLACED with a relative-path symlink and committed, OR (b) scripts/fetch-images-batch.py is changed to read directly from .claude/commands/scripts/google-maps/scripts/places.py (NO symlink dependency). The 'absolute-symlink commit' option is REJECTED.' This removes the latent portability risk.
